subject: Following up from ML Infra Summit — inference fit for Pixly?
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Park <sarah@pixly.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-01T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Intro — ML Infra Summit follow-up

Hi Sarah —

Great to meet you briefly at the ML Infrastructure Summit last week. I enjoyed your talk about low-latency recommendation scoring at Pixly — sounds like you have some interesting real-time constraints. I wanted to follow up and see if youd like to do a short discovery call so we can understand:

- current inference stack (models, frameworks, infra)
- typical request volumes, p95 latency targets, and tail behavior
- data residency/compliance constraints
- cost vs latency priorities for Q2

Are you available for a 30-minute call next Thursday or Friday (Mar 4–5)? Karthik (ccd) is our solutions lead who can join to discuss technical tradeoffs. If a quick calendar invite is easiest, here are two slots I have: Thu Mar 4 10–10:30am PT or Fri Mar 5 11–11:30am PT.

Thanks — happy to be flexible.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
(415) 555-0142

Date: 2026-03-02T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro — ML Infra Summit follow-up

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for reaching out and for the note — great to meet you as well. Thu/Friday both work but Fri Mar 5 at 11am PT is best for our team. Id add Amit (cc) who owns infra at Pixly and will join.

Looking forward to learning more about how Redwood could help reduce per-token inference cost while meeting our tail-latency targets.

See you Friday —
Sarah

sarah@pixly.ai
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Park <sarah@pixly.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-06T14:30:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap + next steps (Pixly / Redwood)

Hi Sarah and Amit —

Thanks for your time on Friday. Quick recap from our discovery and the concrete next steps we discussed: 

Recap (high level):
- Workload: real-time recommendation scoring (batching at front-end, some multi-candidate scoring per user)
- Volume: peak ~18k qps, avg 3k qps; median sequence length ~40 tokens, tail up to 200 tokens for debugging flows
- Targets: p95 latency target 50ms, budgeted cost per 1k requests ~ $2.50 (target)
- Constraints: EU data not in scope yet; US-based infra with SSO + SOC2 requirements

Key next steps we agreed:
1) Id share a one-pager with our suggested deployment patterns for Pixly (attached). It includes model-family tradeoffs, batching/caching recommendations, and an initial cost estimate.
2) Karthik will prepare a short demo runbook to highlight how Redwoodd autoscaling and prefix caching reduce unit cost while maintaining p95.
3) Wed schedule a technical deep-dive with your infra team (30–45m) to validate metrics and iterate on the cost model.

Attached: redwood-inference-pixly-1pager.pdf (one-page summary + rough cost table).
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/12345

Suggested next slots for the technical deep-dive: Wed Mar 10 9–10am PT or Thu Mar 11 1–1:45pm PT. If one of those works Id send a calendar invite.

Let me know if I missed anything critical from your side.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | (415) 555-0142

Hi Sarah —

Just circling back on the one-pager and the technical deep-dive slots I sent last week. Wanted to check whether this is still a priority for Pixly in the next 2–3 weeks, or if timing has shifted. Quick options again: Wed Mar 10 9–10am PT (today) or Thu Mar 11 1–1:45pm PT. If neither works, happy to post a few more windows or connect asynchronously — we can also narrow scope to a focused checklist for your infra team to validate our assumptions.

If it helps, hered my direct calendar link: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=abc123

Thanks — appreciate a quick note on timing.

Best,
Marissa
